leads.nextStep: Confirm whether the study has gone to the board. The project sits under Administrative Services, which is the office to contact.

funding.source: Not identified

leads.headline: District has a staff housing development director and a consultant-led site feasibility study.
leads.summary: Brookwood Partners was hired on a contract of up to $135,000 to find district sites suited to workforce housing, and the district surveyed staff on housing needs. Officials said a project could take five to eight years.

evidence.quote: the actual project could take five to eight years to complete
evidence.source: Marin Independent Journal

leads.nextStep: Feasibility is done; ask what site was chosen and whether a developer solicitation is next.

funding.source: Not identified

leads.headline: Plan for 200+ below-market staff units at Harper Junior High; phase one about 48 units.
leads.summary: The district’s chief strategy officer presented survey results and concept designs, proposing to relocate sports fields to free more than 12 acres. Rents would be 30–50% below market, with funding from property sales or a bond still to be decided.

evidence.quote: the district considers land at Harper Junior High to be the best location
evidence.source: Davis Enterprise

leads.nextStep: Funding path is open. Offer a financing and delivery plan for phase one before a developer solicitation.

funding.source: Property sales or general obligation bonds under consideration

leads.headline: 110-unit staff housing at former Roosevelt Elementary moving through approvals with Education Housing Partners.
leads.summary: The project on 5.3 acres at 315 N. Pasadena Ave. is meant as a prototype for more district sites.

evidence.quote: 110 new rental units exclusively for PUSD teachers and staff
evidence.source: Yield Pro

leads.nextStep: Developer in place. Ask which surplus site is next, since this is billed as a prototype.

funding.source: Measure O bond funds in part

leads.headline: 106 staff apartments on the Tatum parcel; groundbreaking July 2026.
leads.summary: The district sold the Tatum property in 2021 with a condition to preserve land for staff housing, then repurchased a 3.65-acre parcel with developer financing.

evidence.quote: the district repurchased a 3.65-acre parcel for $7.4 million
evidence.source: The Santa Barbara Report

leads.nextStep: Committed. Use as a reference deal for nearby districts.

funding.source: Developer-financed repurchase

leads.headline: 100-unit educator housing at 313 Swift St. broke ground March 2026.
leads.summary: Funded by Measures K and L (2022), about $80 million, opening 2028.

evidence.quote: the first educator workforce housing project in our county’s history
evidence.source: Santa Cruz County Office of Education

leads.nextStep: Committed. Reference deal for other Santa Cruz County districts.

funding.source: Measures K and L bonds

leads.headline: Selling two school-adjacent parcels for 32 for-sale homes with priority for district staff; district calls it a repeatable model.
leads.summary: Bend rezoned a nearly two-acre parcel next to Summit High School in November 2025 for the project with Bend-Redmond Habitat for Humanity. The district owns 72 acres of undeveloped land beyond future school sites.

evidence.quote: The district owns 72 acres of undeveloped land, excluding lots for potential new schools.
evidence.source: OPB

leads.nextStep: With 72 more acres and a stated plan to repeat the model, offer a district-wide land strategy for the next phase.

funding.source: Land sale to Habitat for Humanity

leads.headline: Ten teacher housing units built on district land with an outside advisor.
leads.summary: The district worked with a Prescott Valley investment and advisory firm on land, procurement and financing for employee housing.

evidence.quote: that guidance has led to 10 housing units located on land owned by the Chino Valley Unified School District
evidence.source: Arizona School Boards Association, Partner Link

leads.nextStep: Reference case for other rural Arizona districts; watch for a second phase.

funding.source: Private partner financing

leads.headline: Expanding its 41-unit teacher housing using federal Impact Aid.
leads.summary: The district is putting part of a $10 million federal grant toward an additional unit this year amid statewide teacher vacancies.

evidence.quote: using federal Impact Aid funding to build affordable teacher housing
evidence.source: KOLD 13 News

leads.nextStep: Small, grant-funded expansions; useful for a rural-district housing playbook.

funding.source: Federal Impact Aid

leads.headline: About $180M Ikenberry Commons housing project in late design; procurement expected in 2026.
leads.summary: Part of a broader effort to modernize campus housing; leadership is authorized to proceed to construction procurement once plans are final.

evidence.quote: The project is in the late design stage
evidence.source: Government Market News

leads.nextStep: Procurement is imminent. Ask whether later Ikenberry phases or graduate/family housing are being studied.

funding.source: University housing system

leads.headline: Issued an RFP for a public-private partnership to manage, renovate and potentially build student housing.
leads.summary: NIU sought a concession-style P3 covering existing residence halls and possible new construction, subject to Board of Trustees approval.

evidence.quote: pursue a public-private partnership (P3) arrangement with an established firm
evidence.source: Illinois Public Higher Education Procurement Bulletin

leads.nextStep: Find out whether a partner was selected and whether NIU wants an owner's advisor for negotiation.

funding.source: Public-private partnership
